title: Observation duct: rate-limiting, tenant isolation, and budgeted shadowing
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Problem: We need a safe, observable path to replicate (shadow) production requests to alternate model variants for validation (A/B and canary validation) without causing cost overruns, noisy neighbor effects, or availability regressions. Current ad-hoc mirroring(s) do not enforce per-tenant budgets, allow accidental full-fanout during traffic spikes, and provide poor signal for early rollback decisions.

Goal: Implement an "observation duct" layer in the request plane that centralizes safe-duplication rules: credit-aware sampling, tenant-scoped budget enforcement, request-level tombstoning for large/long-running requests, and clear metrics/alerts that map directly to rollout decisions. This must work across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and integrate with rollout machinery (canaries/A-B and auto-rollback triggers).

Scope:
- Design and implement a lightweight sidecar/edge filter (the Observation Duct) that intercepts requests and decides whether/where to mirror based on tenant budget tokens, sampling policy, and model compatibility.
- Per-tenant budget ledger: token bucket style accounting for shadowed-cost units with soft/hard thresholds and automatic tenant quarantine on hard overrun.
- Multi-mode sampling: deterministic stratified sampling (by route, tenant, request-size, latency percentile buckets) + adaptive sampling that reduces shadow rate under load/cost pressure.
- Request fingerprinting and KV cache hints so shadowed requests reuse cached KV where safe (reduces duplicate compute).
- Safety gates: max-fanout limits, backpressure propagation to avoid cascading latency amplification, and safe-fail behavior (drop shadow copies but always preserve primary response).
- Observability: per-tenant per-model shadowed-token counters, end-to-end tracing linking primary and shadow responses, and dashboard + SLO-based alerts (budget burn rate, error delta between primary and shadow).
- Rollout integration: expose shadow metrics to rollout controller so canaries/A-B tests can be gated by shadow health signals and auto-rollback triggers (error delta > threshold, latency regressions, or unexplained distribution shifts).

Non-goals: implementing new billing pipelines (we will emit usage events for downstream billing) and rewriting runtime kernels.
acceptance_criteria: Observation Duct evaluates and applies sampling rules for 100k requests/min with <2ms median added decision latency
Per-tenant budget ledger enforces soft warning at 75% and hard cut-off at 100% against shadow credits with audit logs
Shadowed requests are limited by a configurable max-fanout and per-route hard limit; primary path unaffected when shadows are dropped
Dashboards show tenant-level shadow burn, shadow-to-primary error delta, and sampling rates; alerts fire on burn-rate > configured threshold
Rollout controller consumes shadow health metrics and can trigger an automated rollback when configured thresholds are exceeded
End-to-end test harness validates that deterministic stratified sampling reproduces sample set across restarts and redeploys

2025-02-21 - Miguel Ortega: Design review notes: require deterministic hashing to ensure sampling reproducibility across restarts; prefer tenant-scoped Redis namespace for dedicated deployments and etcd for private installs. Add explicit API to allow rollout controller to read burn-rate snapshots.

2025-02-27 - Eng QA (L. Gomez): Added test case for large-stream requests — duct should tombstone (not shadow) requests > 2 million tokens or ephemeral jobs; discovered bug where fanout calc double-counted batched requests (PR open).
2025-02-28 - Miguel Ortega: PR #1842 opened for ledger and deterministic sampling. Linked necessary runtime-1.20 feature flag for enablement. Planning staged canary in staging namespace next week.
